final_proof:
Let \(Q=\operatorname{pr}_{M,N}(P)=(u,v)\). A line through the origin whose direction angle is \(\alpha\) has direction vector \((\cos\alpha,\sin\alpha)\). Consequently, if \(\alpha\ne \pi/2\), the line has equation \(Y=X\tan\alpha\), whereas if \(\alpha=\pi/2\), it is the vertical line \(X=0\). We now consider the three possible cases.

If \(\theta=\pi/2\), then \(M\) is the vertical line \(X=0\). Since \(M\ne N\), the line \(N\) is not vertical, so \(\tan\phi\) is defined. The line through \(P=(x,y)\) parallel to \(N\) has equation
\[
Y-y=(X-x)\tan\phi.
\]
Putting \(X=0\), its intersection with \(M\) is
\[
Q=(0,\,y-x\tan\phi).
\]
Thus the first displayed formula holds.

If \(\phi=\pi/2\), then \(N\) is vertical. Distinctness of \(M\) and \(N\) implies \(\theta\ne\pi/2\), so \(M\) has equation \(Y=X\tan\theta\). The line through \(P\) parallel to \(N\) is \(X=x\), and it meets \(M\) at
\[
Q=(x,\,x\tan\theta),
\]
which is the second displayed formula.

Finally, suppose neither \(\theta\) nor \(\phi\) equals \(\pi/2\). Then
\[
M:\ Y=X\tan\theta,\qquad
P+N:\ Y-y=(X-x)\tan\phi.
\]
Because two nonvertical lines through the origin are equal exactly when their slopes are equal, the assumption \(M\ne N\) gives \(\tan\theta\ne\tan\phi\). Hence their intersection \(Q=(u,v)\) is obtained uniquely by solving
\[
v=u\tan\theta,\qquad v-y=(u-x)\tan\phi.
\]
Substitution of the first equation into the second gives
\[
u(\tan\theta-\tan\phi)=y-x\tan\phi,
\]
and therefore
\[
u=\frac{x\tan\phi-y}{\tan\phi-\tan\theta}
 =\frac{x\tan\phi}{\tan\phi-\tan\theta}
  -\frac{y}{\tan\phi-\tan\theta}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
\begin{aligned}
v=u\tan\theta
 &=\frac{x\tan\theta\tan\phi-y\tan\theta}
         {\tan\phi-\tan\theta}\\
 &=\frac{y\tan\theta}{\tan\theta-\tan\phi}
  -\frac{x\tan\theta\tan\phi}
         {\tan\theta-\tan\phi}.
\end{aligned}
\]
These are exactly the two coordinates in the third displayed formula. In every case the two intersecting lines have different directions, so the intersection is unique and is precisely the point specified by the definition of \(\operatorname{pr}_{M,N}(P)\). This proves the stated piecewise formula.
